interpretation: The prospective cross-system role-fraction prediction was supported.

In the microbiome, aligning all communities by the first-arriver role greatly increased retained-history excess, revealing strong colonist-specific differences in how first arrival is expressed structurally.
In the grassland, role alignment added no information beyond rank abundance: role-aligned and rank-abundance targets were exactly identical under the frozen representation.

The v31 storage-mode contrast is therefore consistent with strong asymmetry in first-arriver effectiveness among fungal identities versus a more role-symmetric first-mover-dominance pattern among grassland functional groups.
claim_boundary: Role alignment does not directly identify niche preemption versus niche modification.
Do not call either whole system universally symmetric or asymmetric.
Species-specific variation in priority-effect strength is established in prior literature; v32 links that variation to the present-state storage channel.
